task_instance: Instrument a minimal Node.js/Express web app with Azure Application Insights (OpenTelemetry Distro) per the skill's Node.js manual-instrumentation guidance: add an instrumentation.js entrypoint that initializes @azure/monitor-opentelemetry via useAzureMonitor() before any other module loads, wire it into server.js, add a custom span/event in a route handler, and verify the app starts, the SDK initializes, and requests are served.
evidence: Created work dir with package.json, installed express + @azure/monitor-opentelemetry via `npm install` (network reachable, npm ping succeeded). Wrote instrumentation.js requiring @azure/monitor-opentelemetry and calling useAzureMonitor() guarded by APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING env var (no real secret used). Wrote server.js requiring ./instrumentation first, then express, with a '/' route that opens a custom OpenTelemetry span/event and a '/health' route. Ran `APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING=<synthetic well-formed string> node server.js` in background; server.log showed '[telemetry] Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry Distro initialized' and 'Server listening on port 3000' with no errors. curl http://localhost:3000/ returned 'Hello from an App-Insights-instrumented Node.js app!' and curl http://localhost:3000/health returned {"status":"ok"}, confirming the instrumented app runs and serves traffic with the App Insights SDK initialized without crashing. Deliberately did not attempt to provision a real Azure Application Insights resource or send live telemetry to Azure, since that requires an Azure account/credentials, which is explicitly out of scope for the sandbox and also out of scope for this skill itself (SKILL.md states resource creation/actual app changes should go through a separate 'azure-prepare' skill; this skill is guidance/reference material for how to instrument, which is what was demonstrated and verified).
